newsitem.title: UK: Battle for Congress hobbles U.S. stocks in London.
newsitem.headline: Battle for Congress hobbles U.S. stocks in London.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were flat on Monday as investors fretted over the spectre of President Bill Clinton's Democrats sweeping into both Houses of Congress and unleashing a wave of tax and spend policies.

A day before the U.S. polls, dealers said inflation-wary investors were frantically debating the Republicans' chances to hold on to power in Congress, seen by many as the only way to curb spending excesses and prevent a market rout.
"The principle battle is not presidential. The outcome there is foregone," Roger Monson, strategist at Daiwa Europe, said.

"The question is whether there will be enough coat tails to carry the Democrats in both Houses and Democrat control of all three arms of government may raise concerns about spending and the fiscal side," Monson said.

Monson and U.S. equity dealers in London predicted U.S. stocks were poised to drop if the feared Democrat landslide materialised but said investors were taking heart from polls showing Clinton's lead over challenger Bob Dole narrowing.
"The first reaction will be a little bit on the negative side but we are talking dampened sentiment rather than sell-off. We don't expect a 150-point slide on the Dow," Monson said.

That was echoed by a senior dealer of U.S. equities in London, who said Dole's gains on the back of his marathon last-minute campaign swing were feeding hopes of a respectable Republican showing in Congress.

"We don't see the Democrats sweeping all before them...but worries about the possibility will keep this and the U.S. market tight before the results are known. Sheer relief at any Republican showing might support the market," he said.
Dole's frantic campaigning might be raising momentum for his party but the challenger himself is considered political history, an outcome already factored into markets, experts said.
"Dole doesn't have enough personality to galvanize the broad centre. You'd love him as a neighbour because he'd be so considerate. And that's all he'll be this week," Monson said.
Monson said a Democrat sweep could have some benefits.
"We could see a more pragmatic, less ideological apporach to trade and military for example," he said.
But until the election outcome is known, dealers said markets were likely to maintain a steady, if nervous vigil.
In London, early movers included General Motors, trading higher at $54-3/8, on news workers at a key metal stamping plant in Indianopolis began returning to work.
Other automakers were higher, with Ford up $1/8 at $30-5/8.
Among losers, Boeing was down $3/8 at $91-1/2 amid worries about the implications of a possible move to retro-equip 737 aircraft with rudder movement limiting devices.
Among winners, telecoms giant MCI Communications was up $4-1/4 at $34-1/2, benefiting from its proposed merger with British Telecom.
